Good morning Luca,



London-based Fuse Energy launched with a bang in 2022. It was the climate tech heyday and investors wanted in on the startup, which promised to upend the energy industry by providing customers with clean, cheap energy.



What made the proposition all the more tantalising was the founding team, made up of two former Revolut execs: Alan Chang, third employee at Revolut and widely considered to be CEO Nik Storonsky’s right-hand man, had teamed up with Charles Orr, the fintech’s former strategy lead.



Fast forward three years and Fuse now has a solar plant up-and-running and supplies 200k customers across the UK. Last week, the young company announced a $70m raise, giving it a hefty $5bn valuation.



But the company’s financials for 2024, which were also released last week, along with a delayed US launch, raise questions for the young energy company.
